Database API (v0)

Download OpenAPI specification:Download

API Overview

The API utilizes a RESTful architecture, allowing you to query and manage data from within the AppFolio ecosystem. All API requests and responses are formatted in application/json and HTTP Basic Auth is used to verify a user's identity. Additionally, the base URL for all API requests is https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/{endpoint}.

To kick start your API usage, we recommend diving into our API Getting Started section which takes you step-by-step through a common API use case. Be sure to review the API Best Practices section to optimize your API usage and ensure a seamless integration into your application.

Required Headers

Name Format Value Notes
X-AppFolio-Developer-ID string Developer ID
Authorization string Client ID:Client Secret HTTP Basic authorization. The Client ID and Client Secret must be encoded using Base64.

Authentication

Security Scheme Type HTTP
HTTP Authorization Scheme basic

Rate Limits

To prevent network congestion and avoid 429 Too Many Requests errors, we recommend regulating or staggering the rate of your requests. All endpoints have per-second, per-minute and per-hour rate limits for each set of credentials.
Currently, the rate limits are as follows:

  • 8 requests per second, 256 requests per minute, and 4096 requests per hour

Error Codes

The API returns HTTP status codes. The following error codes are possible.

Error Code Text Description
400 Bad Request The request was not processed due to invalid syntax.
401 Unauthorized HTTP Basic: Access denied.
403 Forbidden The developer has insufficient permissions to access this API endpoint.
404 Not Found The requested resource could not be found.
422 Unprocessable Entity The request was understood, but not processed due to semantic errors. Ensure that the parameters contain valid values.
429 Too Many Requests The developer has sent too many requests.
500 Unexpected Error The server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented a successful request. This is usually a temporary state.
503 Service Unavailable The server cannot handle the request due to overload or maintenance. Please try again later.
533 Data Unavailable Data is currently unavailable. Please try again later.
701 Invalid Credential The customer has restricted access to their data by disabling their API integration.

API Getting Started

Basic GET request using the API

For an API call to be successful in the cURL request below, you must enter a valid resource, Developer ID, and encoded string.

  1. Enter a resource name (e.g. properties, tenants, or charges) that you have been granted access to in the curl request below.
  2. Retrieve your Developer ID by selecting your account name drop-down → Admin → Developer ID in the Developer Details card.
  3. Retrieve your Client ID and Client Secret.
  • Your Client ID can be found by selecting Dashboard → Show Client Id for the desired database.
  • Your Client Secret can be found on the same row by selecting Generate a Client Secret. Store this value in a safe place.
  1. Encode your Client ID and Client Secret in Base64 to generate an encoded string.
  • For Mac users, paste the following command with your Client ID and Client Secret in Terminal:
echo -n "{ClientID}:{ClientSecret}" | base64
  • For Windows users, paste the following command with your Client ID and Client Secret in Windows Command Prompt:
powershell "[convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("{ClientID}:{ClientSecret}"))"
  1. Insert your Developer ID and encoded string (the value returned from the above commands) into the curl command below.
curl -g --request GET 'https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/{resource}?filters[LastUpdatedAtFrom]=2022-06-01T00:00:00Z' \
--header 'X-AppFolio-Developer-ID: {DeveloperID}' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic {encoded-string}'
  1. Copy the full curl request, paste it into your terminal, and click Enter.
  2. A successful request will return a list of the desired resources.

API Best Practices

To maximize efficiency and ensure the reliability of your integration with the API, review the following best practices.

Date and Time Formatting

Our API strictly adheres to the ISO 8601 format for <date-time> representation, which follows the pattern YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ for date and time, where "T" separates the date and time components, and "Z" indicates Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). This global standard ensures clarity and consistency across different systems and programming languages. By following ISO 8601, developers can avoid ambiguity and facilitate seamless integration with our API.

YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ

  • YYYY is the four-digit year

  • MM is the two-digit month

  • DD is the two-digit day

  • T separates the date and time components

  • hh is the two-digit hour

  • mm is the two-digit minute

  • ss is the two-digit second

  • Z indicates Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)

  • 2022-06-00T12:00:00Z is equivalent to June 1st, 2022, at 12:00:00 PM UTC.

Deprecation

When reading the API documentation you will notice attributes marked as Deprecated. When an attribute or endpoint is marked as Deprecated, we no longer recommend using it due to changes in the API.

Any new API users should not use deprecated attributes, and existing API users should consider transitioning to updated attributes or endpoints. When a new API version is released in the future, the deprecated attributes or endpoints will be removed entirely.

Filtering and Pagination

To ensure the proper utilization of the LastUpdatedAt query parameter, we recommend the following best practices:

  • The LastUpdatedAt attribute indicates the date of the most recent update to an object in the AppFolio Property Manager. However, changes may not always be visible to API users, as they could involve internal attributes or attributes that are inaccessible to certain users. API users should not make assumptions about what changed on an object based solely on the fact that LastUpdatedAt has changed. Rather, they should compare the changed object's attributes to the last known attributes to discover the change if needed.

  • For the first import using a given endpoint, you may want to set the LastUpdatedAt filter to a date in the past (e.g. filters[LastUpdatedAtFrom]=1970-01-01T00:00:00Z) and use the response to sync up your internal records. If this response has more than one page, you will need to fetch the following pages as well. For subsequent requests following the initial import, avoid setting arbitrary parameters for LastUpdatedAt and instead set this value to the last time you made a successful request. This will improve performance by only retrieving the data you need, and subsequently reducing the time it takes to receive the response.

To ensure the proper utilization of the page query parameter, we recommend the following best practices:

  • If possible, use the default value for the page query parameter. The default values were carefully selected to ensure that unnecessarily large requests are not sent. The default value for the page size parameter is 1000, but this might differ per endpoint. The page size parameter can be modified to a smaller number if desired. If page sizes larger than the default page size parameter are requested, page size will be reduced to the default value. AppFolio can reduce or increase the default page size parameter for a given endpoint.

The following is an example of a valid request with the default values for the page query parameter:

  • https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/{resource}?filters[LastUpdatedAtFrom]=1970-01-01T00:00:00Z&page[number]=1&page[size]=1000

Outages

As with any API, errors and exceptions will occur. For example, there may be a connection error between servers or a rare outage. Always watch for errors and exceptions, and if they do occur, log the request in as much detail as possible. This will reduce response times in the event that you need to contact support.

  • In the event of a 503 Service Unavailable error, we suggest implementing Exponential Back Off. This ensures that your server does not generate excessive load.
  • A 533 Data Unavailable error typically occurs when a database is down due to database migrations and/or scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance errors will typically resolve within five minutes, and will occur between 9PM and 4AM PST.

Retry-After Header: Retrying Rate Limited API Requests

A Retry-After HTTP response header is utilized by AppFolio to manage rate-limited API requests. When your request is rate limited, this header indicates the time duration in seconds that you should wait before resending the request. It is best practice to observe the value of the Retry-After header and wait for the specified time to resend the request. Adhering to this guidance will reduce the number of 429 "Too Many Requests" errors sent, and conserves resources for both your integration and AppFolio’s services.

Rate Limits and Error Responses:

For each set of credentials, AppFolio enforces rate limits as follows:

  • 8 requests per second
  • 256 requests per minute
  • 4096 requests per hour

Should any of these limits be exceeded, AppFolio will trigger a 429 "Too Many Requests" error and include a Retry-After header.

  • If you send more than 8 requests in a second, the value of the Retry-After header will be 1 second.
  • If you send more than 256 requests in a minute, the value of the Retry-After header will be < 60 seconds.
  • If you send more than 4096 requests in an hour, the value of the Retry-After header will be < 3600 seconds.

Rate Limit Resets and Handling Time-Related Errors:

All rate limits reset at the beginning of each new second, minute, or hour. In scenarios where the per-minute or per-hour rate limits are exceeded, the Retry-After header's value specifies the time remaining until the next complete minute or hour when the 429 Too Many Requests error will expire, and new requests should be sent.

Example Scenario:

For instance, if you sent 300 requests at 09:49:30 AM, the Retry-After header would display 30 seconds. The next request should be scheduled at or after 9:50:00 AM. If the per-hour rate limit is exceeded, the 429 error will expire at the top of the upcoming hour, regardless of the time it was triggered. As an example, sending 5000 requests at 09:15:00 AM would lead to a Retry-After header value of 2700 seconds, necessitating a wait until 10:00:00 AM before you should issue another request.

User Roles

In order to successfully carry out certain requests using the API, the correct user roles must be enabled in the AppFolio Property Manager.

Some examples include:

  • When assigning a lead to a user, that user must have the Leasing Agent role in the AppFolio Property Manager.
  • When creating a work order, the assigned user must have the Maintenance Tech role in the AppFolio property manager.

If a user does not have the correct permissions your request will result in a 422 “User not found.” error.

API Troubleshooting

When troubleshooting issues associated with the API, ensure you can answer Yes to the following questions in the checklist. If you answer No to any of the following questions, it is likely that you have found the problem.

  1. Is the URL correct?
  • A valid URL should look similar to http://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/{endpoint}.
  1. Were the correct credentials passed in the request?
  • Ensure the Client Secret and Client ID belong to the same database whose records you are trying to access.
  1. Is the authorization header valid?
  • Ensure the formatting of the Client ID and Client Secret passed into your authorization header are valid.
  1. Are the correct User Roles enabled?
  • For example, if you are creating a lead and assigning a user to that lead, does the user have the Leasing Agent role enabled?
  1. Are the request parameters valid?
  • If an incorrect parameter value was passed, the returned error codes should be descriptive enough to assist you in identifying the problem.
  1. Is the rate at which you are issuing requests regulated?

  • If multiple PATCH requests are made to the same resource simultaneously, the first request will update the resource but the second request to update the resource will fail. Thus, it is important to spread out or queue your PATCH requests across resources.

  • In general, staggering the rate at which you issue requests will prevent network congestion and errors.

Webhooks Overview

AppFolio provides support for webhooks through the API. Webhooks are HTTP-based callback functions that allow your app to receive real-time updates about events in the AppFolio system. Webhooks are only available for a small subset of endpoints and can be enabled by reaching out to an AppFolio representative.

You must configure a webhook URL to allow your application to receive webhooks. Once a webhook URL is configured, you will subscribe to a specific webhook topic and receive notifications about that event once it occurs in the AppFolio system. For example, when a user creates, updates, or deletes a property within AppFolio, a webhook callback from AppFolio will notify your application about the property event.

Why Use Webhooks?

  • Webhooks provide real-time updates that prevent you from having to periodically query the API, contributing to cost savings in infrastructure and server resources
  • Webhooks make it easier for you to adhere to our rate limits by removing the need to periodically poll for changes
  • Webhooks can allow you to automate workflows in your organization by giving you the ability to define how to respond to webhook event notifications that you receive

Authentication

Webhook event notifications are sent to an endpoint defined and exposed by you. The webhook URL you define must be secured by HTTPS. To validate that the webhook event notifications are coming from AppFolio and verify the integrity of the notification’s content, AppFolio implements JSON Web Signature (JWS) message signing with a detached payload. The X-JWS-Signature header contains the signature for the webhook payload.

You must verify the signature of each webhook and discard all webhook payloads that fail signature verification without processing them. The step-by-step guide to verifying the signature can be found in the Webhooks: Getting Started section along with sample code in several languages.

Authentication Headers

Name Description
X-JWS-Signature An encoded signature that verifies that a webhook event notification came from AppFolio

Webhook Event Payload Structure

The payload of the webhook event notification sent by AppFolio is an HTTP POST request that contains a JSON object with attributes that describe the event that occurred. The following is an example payload AppFolio sends to your webhook when a property has been created in AppFolio. The JSON object contains several attributes explained in the table beneath the example payload.

POST / HTTP/0.0
Host: {your-company-name}.appf.io
Content-Type: application/json
X-JWS-Signature: {encoded-jws-signature}

{"client_id":"{your-client-id}",
"event_id":"0f56aa84-e319-4460-89b2-2be2f6d12345",
"topic":"properties",
"resource_id":"5b4afdd0-25af-11ee-8c46-06b43963c6f4",
"event_timestamp":"2023-03-27T16:55:12Z",
"message_sent_at":"2023-08-28T23:18:27Z"},
“event_type”: ”create”
Attribute Description
client_id Unique identifier of the customer that is sent the webhook event notification. This attribute corresponds to the client_id API credentials used to access that customer via the APIs.
event_id Unique identifier of the webhook event notification sent by AppFolio
topic The topic of the webhook event notification
resource_id Unique identifier of the resource AppFolio is notifying your app about
event_timestamp When the event you were listening for occurred in AppFolio’s system
message_sent_at When AppFolio sent a notification about the event you were listening for
event_type The type of event that triggered the event notification. Valid values include create, update, or delete.

Note: In rare cases, webhooks can be delivered multiple times. Webhook implementations can detect this if needed by checking the event_id attribute for already processed Webhooks and ignoring duplicates. An alternative to detecting duplicates would be to make the operations triggered by the Webhook idempotent. This guarantees that even if an event is triggered multiple times, it will yield the same result if executed only once.

Webhook Event Logs

Webhook event logs include a record of every webhook attempt the AppFolio system has made and information on the success or failure of that call. This can be useful for debugging failed webhook requests, as you can see the event notification's payload and which topic the notification was sent to.

Webhook logs are only accessible by a user with the Administrator role. Webhooks logs are accessible by selecting the Webhooks Logs button from the left navigation or by selecting See All Events from the Webhook Card within Admin Settings. The following table explains the columns present on the Webhooks Logs page.

Log Column Description
Sent At When AppFolio sent the webhook notification about the event
ID Unique identifier of the webhook event notification sent by AppFolio
Topic The topic of the webhook event notification
URL The URL the webhook notification was sent to
Latency The time in milliseconds for the webhook event notification to be sent from AppFolio
Response Code The HTTP response code of the webhook event. A Green status indicates that the Webhook was successful. A Red status code indicates an error stemming from your server.

Webhooks Getting Started

This step-by-step guide walks you through enabling webhooks. The steps include configuring your application to receive notifications, subscribing to webhook topics, and how to start receiving webhook event notifications.

Configure a Webhook URL

The Webhook URL is a server for incoming HTTP POST notification messages triggered by events within the AppFolio system. The URL must be secured by HTTPS, and the domain has to be owned by your company.

  1. Navigate to the Webhook Card within Admin Settings. As a user with the Administrator role, select Admin from the User drop-down in the top-right corner of the page.
  2. Navigate to the Webhooks Card at the bottom left of the page.
  3. To add a Webhook URL, select Edit from within the Webhooks Card. The Webhook URL will become configurable.
  4. Enter the name of your Webhook URL.

Subscribe to Webhook Topics

After webhooks are enabled for your integration, you will be given access to a subset of webhook topics. A webhook topic refers to a specific event or category of events that can trigger a webhook. The topics you can subscribe to will be listed beneath Topic Subscriptions.

  1. From the list of topics available for subscription, select the ones you are interested in enabling by selecting the checkbox adjacent to the webhook topic.
  2. Ensure your Webhook URL can receive an event notification by selecting Send Test Event.
  3. If your Send Test Event was successful, an entry will appear in the webhook logs that the test was successful.
  4. Navigate to the Webhook Logs page and ensure the test event is timed correctly.
  5. The See All Events link will point you to displaying all webhook events you can utilize to debug errant requests.

Important: Once you have subscribed to a topic, it is time to set up your web server to receive HTTPS POST requests from AppFolio. When setting up your web server, ensure that the server is behind the HTTPS URL configured in Step 2.

Verify the Webhook Message Signature

AppFolio signs all outgoing webhooks to enable recipients to verify the authenticity and integrity of the received notifications. You must verify the webhook message signature in the event notification payload sent by AppFolio by executing the following steps. Any notifications that fail the webhook message signature verification must not be processed.

  1. Fetch Public Keys From AppFolio
  • Configure a verification library to obtain public keys from https://api.appfolio.com/.well-known/jwks.json. The endpoint will respond with a set of keys in JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) format:
  1. Read the Payload of the Webhook Request Sent by AppFolio
  • This is a sample request that will be sent to your webhook. Notice the payload and the signature header.
POST / HTTP/1.2
Host: example.appf.io
Content-Type: application/json
X-JWS-Signature: eyJhbGciOiJQUzI1NiIsImlhdCI6MTY5MzI2NDcwNywia2lkIjoiNWViZGMxMjgtMGZmOC00YzRiLTllNzAtZGU3MjBkY2M2ZjEyIiwiY3JpdCI6WyJiNjQiXSwiYjY0IjpmYWxzZX0..CmenfU2_rJqCthg3r2TfbVZmhfCL8j50JOztvKRISkp7su-K5BMd8mbLYJJ2_0l-43W7VzzsYAXd6RD1srjcOcVRVujOik7T9YRd6zdQhzlEjUpcUFXoxXVVj804j0wWY0X9a8TxT-bk6WkmQcu209sj7mT5YfnfkHQSzpVEyjhhwi3oa_NVGMYutrf-Bik-pV-K-as6kfTFd0BTm5SwdFkAtr9La356NcpnQiwGEZ4ethEPjr6VAxiLvxb1d1oSA0U0NawS4ryzMuKk8O0d_64SZo457J9MhgJqfu0j_dPcnz8Hmu1qtleWVPwe7P5cC4o7Ulzwmy70_jxsBs0F4A

{"client_id":"vtnis0cwz9xsnd2yuigactzxpe1s9ggy","id":"0f56aa84-e319-4460-89b2-2be2f6d12345","topic":"work_order_updates","entity_id":"5b4afdd0-25af-11ee-8c46-06b43963c6f4","update_timestamp":"2023-03-27T16:55:12Z","message_sent_at":"2023-08-28T23:18:27Z"}
  1. Extract the JWS Header from the signature. This is before the .. in the X-JWS-Signature header value.
  2. Extract the JWS Signature. This is after the .. in the X-JWS-Signature header header value.
  3. Compute the JWS Payload. Encode the body of the main request (the payload) using the unpadded alternate base64 encoding defined in RFC 4648. Additionally, ensure you are using the unparsed raw contents of the HTTP body, as processing like JSON parsing could reformat the body and cause the verification to fail.
  4. Verify the Webhook Message Signature
  • Concatenate the encoded values from steps 3, 4, and 5 with . as a separator. For example:
jws-header + "." + jws-payload + "." + jws-signature`
  • Pass the JWS Signature, the JWS Header, and the JWS Payload to the JWS verification library you configured with AppFolio's JWKS public keys in Step 1. Code samples in various languages can be found in this repository. This should result in a successful verification.
  • Note: AppFolio uses RSASSA_PSS_SHA_256 as the signature algorithm. For additional information pertaining to this algorithm, click here.

Bill Line Items

Attributes Type Description Notes
Amount String The amount due for the line item Valid format is "DD.CC", e.g. "23.33"
Description String A brief description of the line item
GlAccountId String The general ledger account ID relevant to the line item UUID format e.g. "d9009724-9f32-11ec-bc31-d46a96ab9b08"
PropertyId String The PropertyId associated with the line item. This takes precedence over the top-level PropertyId connected to the bill. UUID format e.g. "d9009724-9f32-11ec-bc31-d46a96ab9b08"
ServiceFrom String The start date of the utility vendor's service Valid format is "YYYY-MM-DD"
ServiceTo String The end date of the utility vendor's service Valid format is "YYYY-MM-DD"
UnitId String The unit ID relevant to the line item UUID format e.g. "914a2a8e-f5d3-11e9-a485-1876da4c83b5"
PostingDate
string <date>

The accrual-accounting invoice date

PropertyId
required
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the property on the bill. If a PropertyId is not found within the LineItem array, use this value for reference purposes.

Reference
string

The reference number of the bill. This number must be unique, no duplicate record is allowed.

Remarks
string

A description or summary of the bill

TotalAmount
required
string <decimal>

The total amount due. Ensure that the total amount is equal to the total of all line items summed.

VendorId
required
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the the payee's vendor ID

WorkOrderId
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the work order corresponding to the bill(s). The value of WorkOrderId cannot be null.

Note: WorkOrderId and AccountNumber are mutually exclusive. Therefore, only one of them can be provided in the request.

PropertyId String The PropertyId associated with the line item. This takes precedence over the top-level PropertyId connected to the bill. UUID format e.g. "d9009724-9f32-11ec-bc31-d46a96ab9b08"
ServiceFrom String The start date of the utility vendor's service Valid format is "YYYY-MM-DD"
ServiceTo String The end date of the utility vendor's service Valid format is "YYYY-MM-DD"
UnitId String The unit ID relevant to the line item UUID format e.g. "914a2a8e-f5d3-11e9-a485-1876da4c83b5"
PostingDate
string <date>

The accrual-accounting invoice date

PropertyId
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the the property associated with the bill. If a PropertyId is not found within the LineItem array, use this value for reference purposes.

Reference
string

The reference number to the invoice number. This number must be unique, no duplicate record is allowed.

Remarks
string

A description or summary of the invoice

TotalAmount
string <decimal>

The total amount due. Ensure that the total amount is equal to the total of all items summed.

VendorId
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the payee's vendor ID

WorkOrderId
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the work order corresponding to the invoice. The value of WorkOrderId cannot be null.

Responses

https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/bills/{billId}

Create Journal Entries

Create a journal entry

Authorizations:
basic_auth
Request Body schema: application/json
required

Journal Entry object

EntryDate
required
string

The date the journal entry was created. Valid format is "YYYY-MM-DD" e.g. "2022-03-03".

required
Array of objects (LineItem)

Array of line-item objects. Two or more line-item objects must be passed to create a journal entry. The sum of the total debits must equal the total credits for all line-item objects.

Journal Entry Line Item

Attributes Type Description Notes
Credit String or null The credit amount Total debits and credits must be equal. For example, if line-item 1 has a credit of "10.00", line-item 2 must have a debit of "10.00".
Debit String or null The debit amount Total debits and credits must be equal. For example, if line-item 1 has a credit of "10.00", line-item 2 must have a debit of "10.00".
Description String A brief, informative description of the journal entry’s line item
GlAccountId String Unique identifier of the general ledger account associated with the journal entry line item
PropertyId
required
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the property or association related to the journal entry

Remarks
string

A description or summary of the journal entry

Responses

https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/journal_entries

Create Community Association Violations

Create a Community Association (CA) Violation

Authorizations:
basic_auth
Request Body schema: application/json
required

Violation object

Description
string

A brief summary or description of the CA violation

InspectionDate
required
string

The date of the CA unit’s inspection

MarkedForEscalation
boolean

Indicates whether or not the CA violation was marked for escalation

UnitId
required
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the unit associated with the CA violation

ViolatedRuleId
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the CA rule that was violated

Status
required
string
Enum: "In Progress" "In Dispute" "Corrected" "On Hold"

Indicates the current status of the CA violation

Status Options

Options Description
In Progress The processing of the CA violation is in progress
In Dispute The CA violation is being disputed by the accused party
Corrected The offense resulting in the CA violation has been corrected
On Hold The proceeding pertaining to the CA violation has been placed on hold

Responses

https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/ca/violations

  • "Description": "sample description",

In Dispute The CA violation is being disputed by the accused party
Corrected The offense resulting in the CA violation has been corrected
On Hold The proceeding pertaining to the CA violation has been placed on hold

Responses

https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/ca/violations/{violationId}

Create Leads

Create a lead

Authorizations:
basic_auth
Request Body schema: application/json
required
AdditionalOccupants
integer

The number of other potential occupants of the residency

AssignedUserId
string <uuid>

The AppFolio Property Manager user responsible for the lead. Reference the Users endpoint for any necessary associations.

Bathrooms
string <decimal>

The number of desired bathrooms

Bedrooms
integer

The number of desired bedrooms

CreatedAt
string <date-time>

The date the lead was created. The value must adhere to the ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ and the default time zone is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

CreditScore
string

The self-reported credit score of the interested party

DesiredMoveIn
string <date>

The date the prospective resident desires to move in

FirstName
required
string

The first name of the interested person

Email
string

The email address of the interested person

HasCats
boolean

Indicates whether or not the interested person has cat(s)

HasDogs
boolean

Indicates whether or not the interested person has dog(s)

HasOtherPet
boolean

Indicates whether or not the interested person has other pet(s)

LastName
required
string

The last name of the interested person

MaxRent
string <decimal>

The max amount the interested person is willing to pay monthly for rent

MiddleInitial
string

The middle initial of the interested person

MonthlyIncome
string <decimal>

The self-reported monthly income of interested person

PhoneNumber
string

The phone number of the interested person

PropertyId
required
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the property associated with the lead

Source
string

The mechanism through which this lead was submitted

Status
string
Enum: "active" "cold" "inactive" "waitlisted"

Indicates the current phase of engagement with a prospective resident

Status Options

Options Description
active A prospective resident is interested in a unit or property
cold A prospective resident has ceased to show interest
inactive A prospective resident is unqualified, or has stated a reason for their lack of interest
waitlisted A prospective resident is interested in a unit or property, but there are currently no units available that fit their interests. If a prospect submits an additional lead, the status will revert to "active"
UnitIds
Array of strings

Unique identifier of the unit(s) that the interested party is interested in

Responses

https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/leads

required
AdditionalOccupants
integer

The number of other potential occupants of the residency

AssignedUserId
string <uuid>

The AppFolio Property Manager user responsible for the lead. Reference the Users endpoint for any necessary associations.

Bathrooms
string <decimal>

The number of desired bathrooms

Bedrooms
integer

The number of desired bedrooms

CreatedAt
string <date-time>

The date the lead was created. The value must adhere to the ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ and the default time zone is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

CreditScore
string

The self-reported credit score of the interested party

DesiredMoveIn
string <date>

The date the prospective resident desires to move in

FirstName
string

The first name of the interested person

Email
string

The email address of the interested person

HasCats
boolean

Indicates whether or not the interested person has cat(s)

HasDogs
boolean

Indicates whether or not the interested person has dog(s)

HasOtherPet
boolean

Indicates whether or not the interested person has other pet(s)

InactiveReason
string (InactiveReason)
Enum: "price" "location" "amenities" "no_response" "decided_not_to_move" "leasing_criteria_not_met" "looking_for_move_in_special" "no_availability" "duplicate" "other"

The reason why the lead was marked inactive

InactiveReason Options

Options Description
price The price caused the lead to be marked inactive
location The location caused the lead to be marked inactive
amenities The amenities caused the lead to be marked inactive
no_response No reason or response was provided
decided_not_to_move The prospective resident decided not to move
leasing_criteria_not_met The prospective resident was unqualified to move
looking_for_move_in_special The prospective resident was looking for a move-in special
no_availability Due to no availability the lead was marked inactive
duplicate The lead was a duplicate
other Other reason(s) not already provided
LastName
string

The last name of the interested person

MaxRent
string <decimal>

The max amount the interested person is willing to pay monthly for rent

MiddleInitial
string

The middle initial of the interested person

MonthlyIncome
string <decimal>

The self-reported monthly income of interested person

PhoneNumber
string

The phone number of the interested person

Source
string

The mechanism through which this lead was submitted

Status
string
Enum: "active" "cold" "inactive" "waitlisted"

Indicates the current phase of engagement with a prospective resident

Status Options

Options Description
active A prospective resident is interested in a unit or property
cold A prospective resident has ceased to show interest
inactive A prospective resident is unqualified, or has stated a reason for their lack of interest If the status is set to inactive, you must specify the reason the lead was marked inactive by setting a value for "InactiveReason"
waitlisted A prospective resident is interested in a unit or property, but there are currently no units available that fit their interests. If a prospect submits an additional lead, the status will revert to "active"
UnitIds
Array of strings

Array of UnitIds to update on the lead. To maintain a unit's association with a lead, pass in that unit's Id.
Passing an empty array of UnitIds will drop all unit interests from the lead.
Passing in null for this array or omitting it from the request will not change the units.

Responses

https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/leads/{leadId}

Update Rental Application

Update a rental application

Authorizations:
basic_auth
path Parameters
rentalApplicationId
required
string <uuid>
Example: 7f3230dc-8b9a-11ec-9b4b-14482e0fbe8e

Unique identifier of the rental application to update

Request Body schema: application/json
required
Status
string
Enum: "approved" "canceled" "decision_pending" "denied"

The rental application's status

Status Options

Options Description
approved The rental application was approved by the landlord/management
canceled The rental application was canceled by the applicant/tenant
decision_pending The rental application's decision is pending
denied The rental application was denied by the landlord/management
StatusReason
string

The reason for the denied or canceled rental application. The StatusReason field is required when the Status of the rental application is denied, and optional when the status of the rental application is canceled.

For all other statuses, such as approved or decision_pending, providing a StatusReason will not be applicable, and the StatusReason will remain null. Updating a rental application from denied or canceled to another status, such as approved, will overwrite the previous StatusReason and result in a null value.

Responses

https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/rental_applications/{rentalApplicationId}

AssignedUserId

Update Showing

Update a showing

Authorizations:
basic_auth
path Parameters
showingId
required
string <uuid>
Example: 7f3230dc-8b9a-11ec-9b4b-14482e0fbe8e

Unique identifier of the showing to update

Request Body schema: application/json
required
AssignedUserId
string <uuid>

AppFolio Property Manager user assigned to the showing. A null value passed to AssignedUserId will unassign the user previously assigned to the showing. Omitting AssignedUserId from the request body will not update the assigned user. Reference the Users endpoint for any necessary associations.

StartAt
string <date-time>

The start time of the showing. The value must adhere to the ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ and the default time zone is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

EndAt
string <date-time>

The end time of the showing. The value must adhere to the ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ and the default time zone is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Notes
string

A brief informative message about the showing

Status
string
Enum: "scheduled" "canceled" "no-show"

The status of the showing

Status Options

Options Description
scheduled The default status once the showing is scheduled
canceled The showing is canceled
no-show The prospective resident did not show

Responses

Update a Portfolio

Update a portfolio

Authorizations:
basic_auth
path Parameters
portfolioId
required
string <uuid>
Example: 9933b9bc-3910-417d-bdf2-8884b63ccf97

Unique identifier of the portfolio to update

Request Body schema: application/json
required

Portfolio object

Name
string

The name of the portfolio

PropertyIds
Array of arrays

Unique identifier(s) of the properties to add or remove from the portfolio.

  • The portfolio you are updating will only include the properties passed in this array.
  • If PropertyIds previously in the portfolio are excluded from the updated array, they'll be added to the Default portfolio in APM
  • A property can only be linked to a single portfolio. If a PropertyId previously associated with another portfolio is passed, it will be removed from that association.

Responses

Create Work Orders

Create a work order which belongs to a property, unit, or occupancy

Authorizations:
basic_auth
Request Body schema: application/json
required

Created work order object

One of
PropertyId
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the property associated with the work order

JobDescription
required
string

A brief description of the work order to be performed

AssignedUsers
Array of arrays

Array of AssignedUsers to create the work order with

Array of objects (BillableItems)

Array of billable line item attributes present on a work order

Billable Item Attributes

Attributes Type Description
Description String A brief informative message about the billable line item
GlAccountId String Unique identifier of the General Ledger account associated with the billable line item
Quantity String The number of services or goods utilized. Must be a positive number
Rate String The rate, or cost, of the goods or services provided
CanceledOn
string <date>

Timestamp of when work order status changed to "canceled"

CompletedOn
string <date>

A timestamp of when the work order status changed to "completed"

Array of objects (LaborItems)

Array of labor line item attributes present on a work order

Labor Item Attributes

Attributes Type Description
Date String The date the labor was completed
Description String A brief informative message about the labor performed
HoursWorked String The number of hours worked by the maintenance tech
HoursBillable String The number of hours worked by the maintenance tech that are billable, used to create the work order bill
UserId String Unique identifier of the maintenance tech assigned to the work order
boolean or string

Indicates whether or not the occupancy has given permission to enter the unit

Priority
string (Priority)
Enum: "Urgent" "Normal" "Low"

The priority of the work order

Priority Options

Options Description
Urgent Highest priority
Normal Normal priority
Low Lowest priority
ScheduledEnd
string <date-time>

When the work order is scheduled to be completed. The value must adhere to the ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ and the default time zone is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

ScheduledStart
string <date-time>

When the work order is scheduled to start. The value must adhere to the ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ.

Status
string (Status)
Enum: "Assigned" "Canceled" "Completed" "New" "Scheduled" "Waiting" "Work Completed"

The status of the work order.

Status Options

Options Description
Assigned The work order has been assigned to an AppFolio Property Manager user
Canceled The work order has been canceled
Completed The maintenance request was closed out
New A new maintenance request
Scheduled The work order to be performed is scheduled
Waiting The work order is pending
Work Completed The work order is completed
VendorId
string <uuid>

Unique identifier of the vendor associated with the work order

VendorTrade
string

The type of service offered by the vendor

Options
Alarm/Security
Appliances

The date the work order was completed

Attributes Type Description

Rate String The rate, or cost, of the goods or services provided
CanceledOn
string <date>

Timestamp of when work order status changed to canceled

CompletedOn
string <date>

Timestamp of when work order status changed to Completed

JobDescription
string

Attributes Type Description

Urgent Highest priority

Low Lowest priority
ScheduledEnd
string <date-time>

When the work order is scheduled to be completed. If ScheduledEnd is null, it will be considered scheduled for 'all day'. The value must adhere to the ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ and the default time zone is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

ScheduledStart
string <date-time>

When the work order is scheduled to start. Set this value together with ScheduledEnd. The time difference between ScheduledStart and ScheduledEnd should not exceed 12 hours unless it is an scheduled for 'all day'. The value must adhere to the ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ and the default time zone is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Waiting The work order is pending
Work Completed The work order is completed

Create Vendor

Create a vendor

Authorizations:
basic_auth
Request Body schema: application/json
required
TaxpayerName
string

The taxpayer name of the vendor
If UseCompanyNameAsTaxpayerName is true, then TaxpayerName will be CompanyName.
If IsCompany is true, and TaxpayerName is not provided, then TaxpayerName will be set to CompanyName.
If IsCompany is false, and TaxpayerName is not provided, then TaxpayerName will be set to the concatenation of FirstName and LastName.
If TaxpayerName is provided, and UseCompanyNameAsTaxpayerName is false, then TaxpayerName will be set as provided value.

TaxpayerId
string

The tax identification number of the vendor. This field accepts either a Employer Identification Number (EIN), a Social Security Number (SSN), or an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN).

CompanyName
string

Optional display name of vendor's company

Send1099
boolean

Indicates whether or not the vendor needs a 1099 tax form from the management company

FirstName
string

The vendor's first name

LastName
string

The vendor's last name

Address1
string

The primary street address of the vendor

Address2
string

Additional street information pertaining to the vendor

City
string

The city where the vendor is located

State
string

The state where the vendor is located (e.g. "CA" for California)

Zip
string

The zip code where the vendor is located

CountryCode
string

The country code of the vendor (e.g. "JP" for Japan)

PhoneNumber
string

The vendor's phone number

Email
string

The vendor's email address

CompanyURL
string

The internet address of the vendor's website

LiabilityInsuranceExpiration
string <date>

The expiration date of the vendor's liability insurance

AutoInsuranceExpiration
string <date>

The expiration date of the vendor's automobile insurance

WorkersCompExpiration
string <date>

The expiration date of the vendor's worker's compensation insurance

ContractExpiration
string <date>

The expiration date of the contract

UmbrellaInsuranceExpiration
string <date>

The expiration date of the vendor's umbrella insurance

CompliantStatus
boolean

Indicates whether or not the vendor meets compliance

NetVendorId
string

The vendor's NetVendor ID

IsCompany
required
boolean

Indicates whether or not the vendor identifies as a company

UseCompanyNameAsTaxpayerName
required
boolean

Indicates whether or not to use the company name for tax paying purposes

Responses

https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/vendors
